subject.title: Feature: channels.slack.ignoreSubtypes config key to suppress message_changed / message_deleted events

question: Should Slack edit/delete events remain documented session-scoped system events, or should OpenClaw add an opt-in `channels.slack.ignoreSubtypes` suppression field for them?
rationale: The requested behavior is source-reproducible, but the fix adds public Slack config surface and chooses event-context policy, which repository guidance treats as maintainer product direction rather than an automatic bug lane.

options.title: Approve narrow opt-in config
options.body: Add `ignoreSubtypes` as a documented Slack plugin config field, keep current behavior as the default, and test that only selected edit/delete subtypes are dropped before session context is queued.

options.title: Change default policy
options.body: Stop queuing edit/delete system events by default, accepting compatibility impact for users who rely on those metadata events as passive context.

options.title: Keep current system events
options.body: Decline the config key and document that edit/delete metadata continues to flow into session-scoped system events.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow opt-in config
recommendation.body: Add `ignoreSubtypes` as a documented Slack plugin config field, keep current behavior as the default, and test that only selected edit/delete subtypes are dropped before session context is queued.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history on the Slack subtype system-event policy and already reviewed the adjacent broad-ignore PR direction.
